title: Resume rules for experienced architects
oneliner: Two pages maximum: profile summary, skills summary, key accomplishments with value, only the projects relevant to this job description, education.
says: For experienced developers and architects preparing a resume: keep it to two pages. Cover a profile summary, a skills summary, key accomplishments showing the value you added to your organization, then project experience - not every project, only the key ones relevant to the job description you are applying for - and education last.
explained: The two-page limit is a forcing function (a constraint that forces the right behavior). Experienced people accumulate twenty years of material, and the instinct to include it all produces a resume where the relevant proof is buried. A screener spends seconds, so the document's job is to make the match obvious: summary says who you are, accomplishments prove value in numbers, and the tailored project list proves relevance to this role.

The tailoring rule connects to his interview-prep reels: the job description is the question paper and the resume is your answer sheet (the job description tells you what they will test; the resume is how you answer). A project list curated per application looks like more work, but it converts better than one static document sprayed everywhere (sent unchanged to every employer) - and for experienced candidates, relevance density is the whole game.
takeaway: Two pages, value-quantified accomplishments, and a project list re-cut for each application. Everything else is dilution.
